newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Grinaker to unbundle two divisions.
newsitem.headline: Grinaker to unbundle two divisions.

text.p: South African industrial holding group Grinaker Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it planned to unbundle its interest in Grinaker Construction and electricity unit Grintek to shareholders.
The move will see 10.3 percent of Grintek unbundled to shareholders.

In August Grinaker said talks on restructuring links to its Siltek unit had ended, but that it was still mulling splitting off construction and a partial rationalisation of the current pyramid structure of the electronics units.
Analysts see unbundling construction as a positive step that will separate it from electronics businesses like Grintek, Siltek and Grinaker Electronics.
The move will separate two fundamentally different sectors that have previously existed within one holding firm and make the group more transparent to investors, they say.
The statement, which has been long awaited by market-watchers, warned the proposed restructuring was conditional upon three elements:
-- The approval by the Commissioner of Inland Revenue (CIR) of both moves in terms of the unbundling legislation.
-- The approval of Grinaker shareholders at a general meeting.
-- The granting of a listing of the Grinaker Construction shares by the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
Grinaker said a more detailed announcement on the restructuring would be made once the approval of the CIR had been received.
"Shareholders of Grinaker and Grintek should therefore continue to exercise caution in their dealings in the shares of these companies," the group cautioned.
